base_override.reason: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH (BDC / investment company): the engine's OCF-based conservative OE is rejected as the base — for an investment company, purchases and sales of loans are operating cash flows, so OCF measures portfolio deployment, not earnings: FY2025 OCF was -$1,717M against net income of +$1,299M, and the OCF-based OE/share was negative in 4 of the last 5 fiscal years (only 1/5 OE-positive years in dcf_numbers.json) for a company that paid a covered $1.92/share dividend in each of those years (net investment income $1,415M / $2.02 per share in FY2025 per the 10-K statements of operations). The result would be a mechanical Tier F. For a BDC, net income is the honest owner's-earnings proxy (the FUTU/LPLA/WSE broker/payments precedent in this sweep): investment income and all expenses including adviser fees and interest are already in it, capex and SBC are filing-proven $0 (see the two overrides), and realized/unrealized gains and losses are a real, if volatile, part of a lender's total return. The median-of-3-FY normalization mirrors the engine's own base method applied to that definition. Declared under bounded authority (c): every input is a figure printed by this run's engine outputs.
base_override.source: Median of the last 3 fiscal years' net income per diluted share, built exclusively from this run's financials_history.csv (engine-filed figures): FY2023 net income $1,522,000,000 / 575,000,000 diluted shares = $2.6470; FY2024 $1,522,000,000 / 624,000,000 = $2.4391; FY2025 $1,299,000,000 / 699,000,000 = $1.8584; median of the three = $2.4391 (the FY2024 value).

moat_against: Product is commoditized credit: senior middle-market loans are replicable by BXSL, Blue Owl, Apollo, other BDCs and returning banks — spread compression directly compresses NII per share

Externally managed: base management and incentive fees are paid to Ares Capital Management — the origination franchise belongs to the adviser, and the fee load is a structural drag on per-share earnings

Measured returns are ordinary and falling: ROE 13.59% / 11.40% / 9.07% over FY2023–FY2025 (fundamentals.json), at or below the cost of equity in the latest year; NAV per share fell $19.94 (FY2025) to $19.35 (Q2 2026)
Leverage and non-cash income: 1.12–1.15x debt/equity amplifies credit losses, and PIK interest/dividends were ~15% of Q2 2026 investment income — earnings quality below the headline

Per-share growth is bought with issuance: share count grew 10.5%/yr (engine) via ATM offerings — portfolio growth has not translated into per-share NII growth (NII/share $2.30 FY2024 → $2.02 FY2025 on the company's reported figures)
moat_for: Largest publicly traded BDC by market cap ($31.2B total assets, FY2025 10-K) — scale in origination, portfolio diversification (hundreds of portfolio companies) and funding access

Ares Credit Group platform: sponsor relationships and direct-lending origination/underwriting infrastructure built since the 2004 IPO; exited investments have generated ~13% asset-level gross IRR since inception (company reporting)

Cheap, termed-out funding: investment-grade unsecured debt access, debt/equity 1.12x at FY2025 within the 0.9–1.25x target range, weighted average stated interest on debt 4.8–4.9% (Q2 2026 presentation)
Dividend durability: $0.48/quarter declared continuously, with a taxable spillover buffer (~$1.38/share per Q2 2026 coverage) covering multiple quarters of payout
Credit record through cycles: non-accruals 2.4% at cost / 1.4% at fair value at Q2 2026, below the ~4% BDC historical average
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat built on scale and sourcing, not on pricing power over a proprietary asset: ARCC is the largest publicly traded BDC ($31.2B total assets at FY2025, 10-K Item 1) and sits inside the Ares Credit Group origination platform, which gives it first-look deal flow, sponsor relationships and underwriting infrastructure a sub-scale BDC cannot replicate, plus investment-grade access to cheap unsecured debt (debt/equity 1.12x at FY2025). The measured return history does not support a higher score: fundamentals.json ROE was 13.59% (FY2023), 11.40% (FY2024) and 9.07% (FY2025) — around, and falling toward, the cost of capital — and the roic_proxy series is null for this filer (no operating-income / invested-capital presentation for an investment company), as is any gross-margin series (a BDC presents total investment income and expenses, not COGS), so no ROIC or gross-margin claim is made. Against the moat: the underlying product (senior loans to sponsor-backed middle-market companies) is commoditized and contested by BXSL, Blue Owl, Apollo and bank re-entry, with spread compression compressing NII; the franchise is rented, not owned — ARCC is externally managed and pays base and incentive fees to Ares Capital Management; and leverage plus PIK income (a material share of investment income) mean credit losses in a downturn hit NAV directly. A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years.
